meta.title: Aimed, Not Dimmed
meta.theme: why the loss of a dark sky is a loss of contrast rather than of darkness, and why the remedy is the direction of a lamp rather than its quantity

format.format_verified: 2026-09: five-sentence TITA jumble, the top-tier variant of the modern CAT default; re-verify against each new official paper

meta.learning_objective: keep a lexical field from doing the work of a reference when every sentence in a set is about the same substance

quality.adversarial_review: Every sentence here contains light, lamps, sky or glow, so surface matching gives a solver no purchase at all and will pair almost any two of them. The live rival joins the sentence about what a dark sky provides to the sentence about aim and amount, because both are statements of principle and both turn on the word 'not': not an absence, not a quantity. That leaves the instruction about aim standing in front of the only description of aiming there is, the shielded lamp that puts its output on the pavement. A second rival opens on the principle about contrast, which is generic and thesis-shaped; it is refused by 'which is what the complaint assumes', since no complaint has been made. A third makes neighbours of the complaint and the lamp, which strands 'that background'.

source.usage_note: Original composition in CAT register for CAT OS. General environmental argument about artificial light at night; no specific town, ordinance, measurement or text adapted or quoted. Personal study only.

meta.reviewer_notes: A premium five-sentence item designed so that the lexical field is useless: light appears in all five sentences. The spine is made of demonstratives and one instruction, and the decoy opener is the sentence stating the principle, whose only tie is a relative clause about a complaint. The inference marker sits in the fourth seat of five and the paragraph closes on a measured result.

sentences.label: A
sentences.text: A lamp that throws half its output above the horizontal raises that background across a whole county, while the same lamp shielded so that all of it lands on the pavement raises almost none of it and lights the pavement rather better.

sentences.label: B
sentences.text: Where that instruction has been followed, the ground is brighter to walk on and the sky above it is measurably darker, which is the combination the brightness complaint says is impossible.

sentences.label: C
sentences.text: Complaints about the night sky are almost always complaints about brightness, and the remedy they propose, fewer and weaker lamps, is the one that does least.

sentences.label: D
sentences.text: What a dark sky offers is not an absence of light, which is what the complaint assumes, but a difference: a faint object is seen because the background behind it is fainter still, and the eye reports ratios rather than amounts.

sentences.label: E
sentences.text: The useful instruction is therefore about aim and not about amount, and a town that halved its lamps without aiming them would lose the light it wanted and keep the glow it did not.

links.explanation: 'Which is what the complaint assumes' names a complaint, and the only complaint in the set is the one about brightness and its proposal of fewer and weaker lamps.
'That background' points at a background already defined, and it is defined one sentence earlier as the thing a faint object has to be seen against. Nothing else in the set introduces one.
'Therefore' draws on the contrast just made between an unshielded lamp and the same lamp shielded, which is the only evidence in the paragraph that direction matters more than quantity.
'That instruction' names an instruction, and the only one given anywhere is to attend to aim rather than amount. Without it the closing sentence reports compliance with nothing.

explanation.macro_pattern_note: A misdiagnosed problem, the correct account of what is being lost, the mechanism that shows where the loss comes from, the instruction the mechanism licenses, and finally the result where the instruction has been followed. Five moves, each depending on the one before, in a paragraph where the vocabulary is identical throughout and therefore tells the solver nothing.

movement.label: C
movement.why_here: It states the complaint and the remedy the complaint suggests, and it is the only sentence that introduces its subject rather than referring back to it. Two later sentences point at this complaint by name.

movement.label: D
movement.why_here: The correction. It replaces brightness with contrast, and it introduces the background that the next sentence raises. Its relative clause, about what the complaint assumes, is what keeps it out of the first seat.

movement.label: A
movement.why_here: The mechanism, and the only place in the paragraph where two lamps are compared. 'That background' fixes it immediately after the sentence that defines one, and the comparison it makes is what the instruction is drawn from.

movement.label: E
movement.why_here: The instruction, and the nucleus. Its 'therefore' draws the inference in the fourth seat of five, and the warning about halving lamps without aiming them answers the remedy proposed in the opening sentence.

movement.label: B
movement.why_here: The result, and the close. 'That instruction' can only be the one just given, and the paragraph ends on a measurement, brighter ground, darker sky, rather than on a verdict.

tempting_orders.why_tempting: The sentence about contrast and the sentence about aim are the two statements of principle, both built on the same rhetorical frame, not an absence but a difference, not amount but aim, and every sentence in the set shares the vocabulary of light, so nothing in the surface argues against putting the two principles together and treating the lamp as the illustration afterwards.
tempting_orders.where_it_breaks: The instruction says a town that halved its lamps 'without aiming them' would keep the glow. Aiming has not been described at that point: the only description of it is the shielded lamp whose output lands on the pavement, and this order places that sentence after the instruction drawn from it. The 'therefore' would also be inferring from nothing.

tempting_orders.why_tempting: 'The complaint' reads like the general definite of a writer naming a grievance his readers already have, everybody has heard people complain about the night sky, so the clause looks like a reference to the world rather than to a sentence. The rest of the line is the paragraph's idea stated generically, which makes it an inviting thesis.
tempting_orders.where_it_breaks: The sentence contains 'which is what the complaint assumes'. In the first seat there is no complaint, and the definite article cannot reach forward to the sentence that makes one. A correction also needs the error stated before it, or the reader does not know what is being corrected.

tempting_orders.why_tempting: The complaint is about lamps and the mechanism sentence is about a lamp, so the two look like a natural pair: the grievance, then the physical detail behind it. The sentence about contrast then reads as the theory that follows.
tempting_orders.where_it_breaks: The mechanism sentence says the unshielded lamp 'raises that background'. No background has been mentioned, because the sentence that defines one, the fainter thing a faint object is seen against, is the sentence this order jumps over. A demonstrative with nothing behind it is the clearest evidence a jumble offers.

explanation.trap_named: The trap is a paragraph in which the lexical field is worthless. Light, lamp, sky, bright, dark and glow appear everywhere, so a solver who joins sentences by shared words can join any two and will trust whichever pairing he tried first. What remains usable is a small set of pointing words: 'the complaint', 'that background', 'that instruction'. Each of them has exactly one possible antecedent, and together they give the whole order without a single appeal to how well two sentences read side by side.
explanation.solving_habit: When every sentence is about the same thing, stop reading for topic and read for pointers. List each demonstrative and definite phrase, find its one possible antecedent, and let the chain assemble itself.

mentor.challenge: All five sentences are about light, so the shared words tell you nothing. Three pointing phrases tell you everything.
mentor.paragraph_plain: Complaints about the night sky are nearly always complaints about brightness, and the remedy they suggest, fewer and weaker lamps, is the one that achieves least. What a dark sky gives you is not an absence of light, which is what the complaint assumes, but a difference: you see a faint object because the background behind it is fainter still, and the eye works in ratios rather than in amounts. A lamp that throws half its output above the horizontal lifts that background across a whole county, while the same lamp shielded so that everything lands on the pavement lifts almost none of it and lights the pavement better. The useful instruction is therefore about aim rather than amount, and a town that halved its lamps without aiming them would lose the light it wanted and keep the glow it did not. Where that instruction has been followed, the ground is brighter to walk on and the sky above it is measurably darker, which is exactly the combination the brightness complaint says cannot happen.
mentor.takeaway: When every sentence shares a vocabulary, only the pointing words are evidence.
